target_customer: Small and mid sized online businesses, SaaS companies and ad agencies that wanted self-service retargeting ads
problem: Most website visitors leave without buying, and retargeting was run by sales led ad networks aimed at large advertisers. Small businesses wanted a cheap self-service way to bring visitors back.
business_model: Self-service ad platform charging by usage, with CPM based media spend and a platform fee

founders.name: Brad Flora
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is now a General Partner at Y Combinator and was previously CEO and co-founder of Perfect Audience.

founders.name: Jordan Buller
founders.background_notes: YC page lists the CTO as Jordi Buller; TechCrunch coverage spelled it Jordan Buller. No further background in opened sources.

competitors.name: Criteo
competitors.what: Display retargeting, self-service CPC bidding platform launched September 2010
competitors.traction_then: called the largest retargeting company in a 2011 trade article

competitors.name: FetchBack
competitors.what: Retargeting with a self-service interface, owned by GSI Commerce after 2010

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a tracking pixel, high volume ad serving and bidding integrations with ad exchanges. Standard but demanding engineering for a team of two or three, later extended to Facebook Exchange.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals sold the same service and ad exchange access was open to all, so the moat was price and ease of use. The company later benefited from early access to Facebook Exchange.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors kept growing, but none bought it early. Marin Software bought it in June 2014 for about $22.8M, mostly in stock, and sold it to SharpSpring in November 2019 for about $4.6M.

market_need_then: Retargeting spend was growing in 2011 and a 2011 trade article described Criteo as the market leader, while self-service options for smaller advertisers were limited. YC's blog later cited about 2,500 advertisers and over 4 billion ad impressions per month.

branding.domain_note: Used perfectaudience.com; the domain did not resolve in this session's network.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, benefit driven pitch aimed at tech bloggers and small advertisers

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage at the 2012 launch and Facebook Exchange coverage; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in ad tech trade press, but a descriptive name and no sourced evidence of a distinctive identity or community.

outcome_analysis: Perfect Audience offered cheap self-service retargeting and added Facebook Exchange, reaching about 2,500 advertisers on a small seed of roughly $1.1 million. Marin Software bought it in June 2014 for about $22.8 million, mostly stock, but the unit was later sold to SharpSpring in 2019 for about $4.6 million, so the exit value declined as Marin's stock and focus weakened.
